g.text: Young cyclists: how to read the numbers

text.style: font-size: 11.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: A companion to the chart of deaths and hospital stays. The counts are small. That is not the same as a small risk.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 14.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: What the counts show

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 14.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: What the counts cannot show

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 14.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: What other studies add

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: Few deaths, and fewer than before
Cyclists under 15 killed in Canada, by five-year
period:

g.text: Almost all of them in traffic
31 of the 34 killed in 2015–2024 were in a collision
with a motor vehicle.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: Many more injuries than deaths
615 hospital stays a year under 18, 106 of them in
the table of brain injuries, against about 3 deaths
a year under 15.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: The risk
No source measures how much children cycle, or how
much of it is in traffic. A low count can mean safe
streets, or few children riding in them.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: Why the deaths fell
The table gives no cause. Safer streets, less riding
in traffic, helmets and better trauma care are all
possible.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: Injuries outside the hospital ward
About 5 % of cyclists’ emergency visits end in
admission, and police reports capture about a tenth
of hospital-treated injuries (all ages).

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: A city
These are national totals. No public source gives
deaths or hospital stays of child cyclists for
Montréal.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: Per kilometre, the risk is high
On trips between home and school in the Montréal
area, children aged 5 to 12 were injured 22.2 times
as often per kilometre by bicycle as by car, mostly
with minor injuries.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: A motor vehicle makes it worse
In one study of young cyclists, a collision with a
moving motor vehicle multiplied the odds of hospital
admission by 4.17.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: Children’s heads
In Québec the rate of hospital stays with a head
injury is about three times higher among children
than among adults.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.4px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: The charts show how often the worst outcomes are recorded. They do not show how safe a street is for a child on a bicycle.

Sources: deaths, Statistics Canada, table 13-10-0156-01 (cyclists, ICD-10 V10–V19, ages under 15; grouping of codes by this review; pedal cycles only: riders of electric scooters are counted as pedestrians, riders

of electric bicycles as motorcyclists). Hospital stays and emergency visits, Canadian Institute for Health Information, injury and trauma tables 2024–2025. Police reports, Toronto (PMID 38195658). Home-to-school

trips, Montréal area, 2003–2007 (PMID 25408178, abstract). Odds of admission, one study in a systematic review of risk factors in children (PMID 27940760). Québec rates and the remark that exposure data are almost
non-existent, Institut national de santé publique du Québec, La sécurité des cyclistes (2018).
